clarity.justification: The method aligns with the hypothesis by proposing to "Compare raw vs fair-lens dominant-language attribution by layer/language" and measuring "raw vs fair-lens dominant-language token fraction by layer," with the directional prediction that calibration will reveal "substantially more language-neutrality (or target-language content)." However, the central intervention is underspecified because "per-language unembedding calibration (whitening / learned readout)" names materially different methods without defining their training objectives, data, or what formally constitutes a language-neutral attribution, while "agreement of fair lens with causal concept probes" is likewise not operationalized. The claim is nevertheless refutable in principle: failure to reduce dominant-language attribution relative to the raw lens, or failure to agree better with the proposed causal probes, would contradict its prediction, although no numeric effect threshold is supplied and the disjunction "language-neutrality (or target-language content)" weakens decisiveness.

feasibility.justification: Raw logit-lens extraction, whitening, learned linear readouts, and the stated comparisons are supported by standard activation-hooking and machine-learning tooling, but the hardest step—"Validate fair lens against causal concept probes (which language's content is causally present)"—is not defined sufficiently to determine the intervention, measured causal effect, or language-specific control, making it closer to a magic step than a ready operation. Logit-lens methods and multilingual models exist, but the proposal names no exact model, dataset, language set, calibration sample, or implementation of the proposed causal probe; it also provides no concrete sample-size or other resource figures. The controls "dominant-language inputs (should read dominant either way); random calibration" make a negative result possible and help detect overcorrection, but they do not resolve the missing matched-language, concept, and calibration specifications needed to interpret that result rigorously.
